title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. On the previous page Grothendieck set up a general formalism. A stratification of a space X is a locally finite partition (X_i^*) indexed by a preordered set I. Equivalently it is a map φ: X→I, with I given the specialization (Alexandrov) topology and X_i = ∪_{j≤i} X_j^* closed. He compared conditions on such data: 1°) the topology of I is the quotient topology; 3°) φ is open, i.e. the closure of X_j^* is a union of strata (frontier condition); 4°) X_i^* ≠ ∅. He showed that 'stratifying partitions' are the same as 'strict stratifications'. These are increasing locally finite families of closed sets X_i with (1°) covering X, (2°) X_i∩X_j = ∪_{k≤i,j} X_k, (3°) X_i^* ≠ ∅ and (4°) X_j rare in X_i for j<i, i.e. X_i is the closure of X_i^*.

This page has three parts.

(A) Top left: a lemma on open maps. φ: X→Y is open iff for all B⊂Y, φ^{-1}(cl B) = cl(φ^{-1}B), and only the inclusion ⊂ matters. He unwinds this pointwise: φ(x) ∈ cl B ⇒ every neighbourhood U of x has φ(U)∩B ≠ ∅. Equivalently, for every open U, every y∈φ(U) and every B with φ(U)∩B = ∅, y ∉ cl B; that is, φ(U) is open. This is exactly the tool for translating 'φ open' into 'closure of a saturated set is saturated', as used on p.3.

(B) Left, §5: functoriality of the axioms.
- 1° and 2° are stable under arbitrary pullback X'→X.
- 3° (non-empty strata) is not stable, not even under open embeddings.
- 4° (density) is not stable under arbitrary pullback, but is stable under restriction to an open set and under sums.
- He introduces 'fidelity' 3°bis: X_i ⊂ X_j ⇒ i ≤ j, so the order of I is the inclusion order of the X_i. He notes that fidelity does not imply non-empty strata. Example: I={a,b,c} with a,b<c and X_c = X = X_a ⊔ X_b, X_a, X_b ≠ ∅. This is faithful, yet X_c^* = ∅.
- Assuming 1°, 2°, 3°bis, restriction to an open U gives (U_i = X_i∩U) indexed by I_U = {i : U_i ≠ ∅}, a 'pseudo-faithful' stratification of U.
- Strict stratifications restrict to strict ones. This is correct: if U meets X_i = cl(X_i^*), then U meets X_i^*.
- Hence pseudo-faithful stratifications of the open sets of X form a presheaf, whose sections are called 'local stratifications'. This is the first step toward a sheaf or stack of stratifications.

(C) Right: analysis of condition 1° (I carries the quotient topology), for I finite.
- He takes J non-closed with X_J^* closed and J minimal.
- Then for j∈J with cl{j} ⊄ J, the set J∩cl{j} is again a counterexample, since X^*_{J∩cl j} = X_J^* ∩ X_j is closed. By minimality J ⊂ cl{j}, so J has a greatest element j.
- Every other j'∈J has cl{j'} ⊂ J, so J = J_0 ⊔ {j} with J_0 closed.
- Since X_J^* = X_{J_0} ⊔ X_j^* is closed, the frontier X_j^• := cl(X_j^*) \ X_j^* lies in X_{J_0}, yet cl{j} ⊄ J_0∪{j}.
- A second minimisation over I' = cl(J) gives the inductive hypothesis that the property holds on cl{j}\{j}.
- Conclusion, as equivalent conditions: (7) X_J^* closed ⇒ J closed; (8) X_L^* open ⇒ L open; (9) a local, frontier-type criterion. If the frontier of X_j^* lies in X_{J_0} with J_0 closed (WLOG J_0 ⊂ cl{j}), then J_0∪{j} is closed, i.e. cl{j} ⊂ J_0∪{j}. This is checked inductively along cl{j}\{j}.
- So the quotient-topology condition is reduced to a stratum-by-stratum condition on frontiers.

Purpose: an axiomatics of stratified spaces as maps to posets with good topological properties, functorial and local, preparing the 'déploiement' / conical-neighbourhood theory in tame topology.
errors: The garbled sentence 'pour tout K⊂I, K fini et K∩J non fermé, i.e. K⊃J' only makes sense with K closed (K = cl{j}): for closed K with K∩J non-closed, minimality forces K∩J = J. With 'fini' the argument does not run.

Gap: the claim that restriction to an open U yields a stratification that is only 'pseudo-faithful' is not justified on the page. Fidelity (X_i∩U ⊂ X_j∩U ⇒ i≤j) can indeed fail after restriction, and 'pseudo-fidèle' is not defined here.

The equivalence of 7)–9) is sketched only for finite I, and the inductive part of 9) is stated rather than proved. The core minimal-counterexample argument (J has a greatest element, J_0 is closed, the frontier lies in X_{J_0}) is correct.

ideas.what: Characterization of open maps: φ open iff φ^{-1}(cl B) ⊂ cl(φ^{-1}B) for all B
Stability of stratification axioms (covering, intersection, non-empty strata, density) under pullback, open restriction and sums; counterexample showing fidelity does not imply non-empty strata
ideas.modern_name: functoriality / base change of poset-stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; cf. Lurie, Higher Algebra App. A (P-stratified spaces, pullback stability)

ideas.what: Presheaf of (pseudo-faithful) stratifications on the opens of X; its sections called 'local stratifications'
ideas.modern_name: presheaf/sheaf (stack) of stratifications; germs of stratifications
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; implicit in germ-of-stratification arguments in singularity theory (Mather, Thom)

ideas.what: Reduction of the quotient-topology condition for φ: X→I to a local frontier criterion via a minimal counterexample with a greatest element
ideas.modern_name: quotient (Alexandrov) topology criterion for poset-stratifications; frontier condition
ideas.usually_credited_to: frontier condition: Whitney/Thom/Mather; poset-valued stratifications: Lurie (HA App. A), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 only mentions stratified structures/tame topology in general

missed.claim: Around 1981 Grothendieck formalizes stratifications as maps φ: X→I to a preordered set with its specialization topology. He studies continuity, openness (equivalent to the frontier condition) and the quotient property, and how these behave under pullback and open restriction. This anticipates the 'P-stratified space = continuous map to a poset with Alexandrov topology' formalism of Lurie (Higher Algebra App. A, c.2009–2017) and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka. In that literature the formalism is not traced to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: les strat. ps. fidèles des ouverts de X forment un préfaisceau, dont les sections sont appelées les stratifications locales
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It provides a historical precedent for the poset-map approach to stratified homotopy theory (exit paths, constructible sheaves). The fine distinctions here (fidelity vs. non-empty strata, quotient vs. open, stratification vs. strict stratification) are exactly the subtleties that the modern literature handles ad hoc.

missed.claim: The 'local stratifications' presheaf is introduced but its gluing or sheafification is not carried out on this page. The criterion 9) for the quotient topology is reduced inductively but not completed in general (infinite, locally finite I).
missed.quote: Conditions équiv. 7) X_J^* fermé ⇒ J fermé 8) X_L^* ouvert ⇒ L ouvert 9) ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A sheaf/stack of stratifications, with a clean local criterion for the stratifying map to be a quotient, is relevant to defining stratified spaces up to refinement and to tame-geometry versions of Grothendieck's 'déploiement' programme.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly careful point-set bookkeeping. Its interest is that it shows Grothendieck already working with the stratification-as-map-to-poset formalism, its functoriality and a presheaf of local stratifications, years before this became standard. Nothing deep is proved here.
transcription_corrections: Right column: 'Disons J tel que X_J fermé' should read X_J^* fermé (starred).
'pour tout K⊂I, K fini et K∩J non fermé, i.e. K⊃J' — likely 'K fermé', i.e. for closed K, K∩J non-closed ⇒ K⊃J.
'i.e. J est plus grand el. de J' should be 'j est plus grand élément de J'.
Example on the left: I = {a,b,c} drawn with a,b < c (arrows to c), X_c = X = X_a ⊔ X_b.
Top right marginal: 'Prenons J minimal' (written above the struck-out attempt).
Garbled passage in §5 about 'individualisations' is likely about stability of 4°) under sums/restriction to opens, and its failure under general pullback; the transcription repeats phrases.
